The '''21st Academy Awards''' were held on March 24, 1949, honoring the films of [[1948 in film|1948]]. The ceremony was moved from the Shrine Auditorium to the Academy's own theater, primarily because the major Hollywood studios had withdrawn their financial support in order to address rumors that they had been trying to influence voters.<ref>Freeman, B. (1999, Mar 21). [https://www.proquest.com/docview/421559183 "OSCARS '99; unforgettable in every way; A winner's wife recalls the excitement of the awards in 1949, despite that year's humble venue."] ''Los Angeles Times''</ref> This year marked the first time a non-Hollywood production ([[Laurence Olivier]]'s ''[[Hamlet (1948 film)|Hamlet]]'') won Best Picture, and the first time an individual (Olivier) directed himself in an Oscar-winning performance.

The [[Academy Award for Best Costume Design]] was introduced this year.<ref name="oscars.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.oscars.org/oscars/ceremonies/1949/memorable-moments |title=The 21st Academy Awards Memorable Moments |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]]}}</ref> Like [[Academy Award for Best Cinematography|Best Cinematography]] and [[Academy Award for Best Production Design|Best Set Decoration]], it was split into Color and Black & White categories.

[[John Huston]] directed his father, [[Walter Huston]], to the [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor]] for his role as Howard in ''[[The Treasure of the Sierra Madre (film)|The Treasure of the Sierra Madre]]'', a unique accomplishment. The Huston family won three Oscars that evening (John won for [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] and [[Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay|Best Screenplay]], both for the same film). [[Humphrey Bogart]]'s lack of a nomination for Best Actor has been since considered one of the Academy's greatest slights.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.ew.com/ew/gallery/0,,20007870_20164474_20179108_22,00.html |title=100 Worst Oscar Snubs Ever: Humphrey Bogart, The Treasure of the Sierra Madre |author=Entertainment Weekly |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |access-date=2009-09-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227040930/http://www.ew.com/ew/gallery/0%2C%2C20007870_20164474_20179108_22%2C00.html |archive-date=2009-02-27 }}</ref><ref name=dirks>{{cite web|url=http://www.filmsite.org/aa48.html |title=1948 Academy Awards Winners and History|publisher=FilmSite.org ([[American Movie Classics]]) |first=Tim |last=Dirks |access-date=2009-09-01 | archive-date=April 19, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150419062852/http://www.filmsite.org/aa48.html | url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[Joan of Arc (1948 film)|Joan of Arc]]'' set a record by receiving seven nominations without being nominated for Best Picture; this stood until ''[[They Shoot Horses, Don't They? (film)|They Shoot Horses, Don't They?]]'' ([[1969 in film|1969]]) received nine nominations at the [[42nd Academy Awards]] without one for Best Picture. [[Walter Wanger]], producer of the film, was not pleased to see the film avoid a Best Picture nomination, and turned down a special Oscar designed to make up for this slight.<ref name="Oscars '48 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/838/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=838 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref>

''Hamlet'' became the fifth film to win Best Picture without a screenwriting nomination; the next to do so would be ''[[The Sound of Music (film)|The Sound of Music]]'' at the [[38th Academy Awards]]. [[Jane Wyman]] became the first performer since the silent era to win an Oscar for a performance with no lines;<ref name=dirks /> ''Johnny Belinda'' was the fourth film to receive [[List of films with all four Academy Award acting nominations|nominations in all four acting categories]].

In addition, ''[[Johnny Belinda (1948 film)|Johnny Belinda]]'' set the record for most Oscars lost with 11 (1 for 12). It has since been tied with ''[[Becket (1964 film)|Becket]]'' (1 for 12), ''[[The Turning Point (1977 film)|The Turning Point]]'' (0 for 11), ''[[The Color Purple (1985 film)|The Color Purple]]'' (0 for 11), ''[[The Power of the Dog (film)|The Power of the Dog]]'' (1 for 12), and ''[[Emilia Pérez]]'' (2 for 13). However, its record was broken at the [[98th Academy Awards]] by ''[[Sinners (2025 film)|Sinners]]'' (4 for 16).

''[[I Remember Mama (film)|I Remember Mama]]'' received four acting nominations but not one for Best Picture, tying the record set by ''[[My Man Godfrey]]'' in [[9th Academy Awards|1936]]. Two more films to date have tied this record: ''[[Othello (1965 British film)|Othello]]'' ([[38th Academy Awards|1965]]) and ''[[Doubt (2008 film)|Doubt]]'' ([[81st Academy Awards|2008]]).

===Special Foreign Language Film Award===
*To ''[[Monsieur Vincent]]'' ([[France]]) - voted by the Academy Board of Governors as the most outstanding foreign language film released in the United States during 1948.

===Special awards===
*To [[Ivan Jandl]], for the outstanding juvenile performance of 1948, as Karel Malik in ''[[The Search (1948 film)|The Search]]''.
*To [[Sid Grauman]], master showman, who raised the standard of exhibition of motion pictures.
*To [[Adolph Zukor]], a man who has been called the father of the feature film in America, for his services to the industry over a period of forty years.
*To [[Walter Wanger]] for distinguished service to the industry in adding to its moral stature in the world community by his production of the picture ''[[Joan of Arc (1948 film)|Joan of Arc]]''.
*To [[Jean Hersholt]] - in recognition of his service to the Academy during four terms as president.

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
*[[Jerry Wald]]
